'''Mauro Francaviglia''' (22 June 1953 – 24 June 2013) was an Italian [[mathematician]].

He was a professor at [[University of Turin]] and he worked mainly on [[Differential geometry|geometric]] methods applied to [[mechanics]], [[mathematical physics]] and [[general relativity]].

==Biography==
Francaviglia obtained a degree in Mathematics at [[University of Turin]] in 1975 under the supervision of [[Dionigi Galletto]]. In the same university, he was a fellow of the [[National Research Council (Italy)|CNR]] (the Italian National Research Council) from 1975 to 1978 and a teaching assistant from 1978 to 1980. In 1976 he was awarded the Bonavera Prize from the {{ill|Accademia delle Scienze di Torino nel 1977|lt=Accademia delle Scienze di Torino nel 1977|it}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Premio Bonavera|url=https://www.accademiadellescienze.it/attivita/premi-e-borse/premi-del-passato/premio-bonavera|access-date=2021-07-17|website=accademiadellescienze.it}}</ref>

He became full Professor at University of Turin in 1980, when he was 27&nbsp;years old (the youngest full professor in his discipline).<ref>{{cite journal|title=Obituary of professor Mauro Francaviglia|author=M. Ferraris|journal=Int. J. Geom. Methods Mod. Phys.|volume=11|issue=2|year=2014|pages=1477001 (2 pages)|display-authors=etal|doi=10.1142/S0219887814770015|doi-access=}}</ref> He spent the last years of his life at the [[University of Calabria]], in Arcavacata di Rende.

Besides his scientific activities, Francaviglia was a prominent [[Philately|philatelist]]. He has been president of the Unione Filatelica Subalpina di Torino,<ref>{{Cite web|title=La storia dell' Unione filatelica Sub Alpina|url=http://www.filateliasubalpina.it/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=46&Itemid=68|access-date=2021-07-17|website=filateliasubalpina.it}}</ref> vice-president of the {{ill|Federazione tra le società filateliche italiane|lt=Federazione tra le società filateliche italiane|it}}, council member of the {{ill|Unione stampa filatelica italiana|lt=Unione stampa filatelica italiana|it}}, member of the [[Royal Philatelic Society London]] and council member of the {{ill|Académie européenne de philatélie|lt=Académie européenne de philatélie|fr}}.<ref>{{cite web|date=|title=Vaccari news quotidiano di filatelia, posta e collezionismo|url=http://www.vaccarinews.it/index.php?_id=14613&_print=1|publisher=Vaccarinews.it|accessdate=2013-07-17}}</ref>

== Research ==
Francaviglia's scientific interests covered a wide range of topics, including the application of [[differential geometry]] in [[mathematical physics]], [[classical mechanics]], [[general relativity]] and [[Field theory (physics)|field theories]], [[calculus of variations]], [[symmetries]] and [[conservation laws]], [[quantization (physics)|quantization]] and [[thermodynamics]].

He was author of over 250 papers,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mauro Francaviglia's research works {{!}} Università degli Studi di Torino, Turin (UNITO) and other places|url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Mauro-Francaviglia-55894947|access-date=2021-07-17|website=ResearchGate}}</ref> three monographs and 11 encyclopaedia long entries, and he supervised 6 PhD students.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mauro Francaviglia - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=51282|access-date=2021-07-17|website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref>

He was director of several courses at {{ill|Centro internazionale matematico estivo|lt=Centro internazionale matematico estivo|it}}; he organized 20 national and international conferences, among which the 14th World Conference on General Relativity in [[Florence]] (1995).<ref>{{Cite web|title=INSPIRE|url=https://inspirehep.net/conferences/968944|access-date=2021-07-17|website=inspirehep.net}}</ref>

He was member of the Scientific Council of the [[INdAM]] National Group for Mathematical Physics (GNFM) (1980–1996) and life member of the [[International Society on General Relativity and Gravitation|International Society on General Relativity]]. In 1990 he founded the [[Italian Society for General Relativity and Gravitation]] (SIGRAV), of which he was president for two terms (1992–1996 and 2008–2012). He also served as a member of the Board of the [[International Society on General Relativity and Gravitation]] (IGRG) for nine years (1986–1995).

Francaviglia was co-founder (1984) and Managing Editor of ''[[Journal of Geometry and Physics]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|title=Editorial Board - Journal of Geometry and Physics - Journal - Elsevier|url=http://journals.elsevier.com/journal-of-geometry-and-physics/editorial-board|access-date=2021-07-17|website=journals.elsevier.com}}</ref> Associate Editor of the ''[[General Relativity and Gravitation|Journal of General Relativity and Gravitation]]'' since 1999 and Managing Editor of the ''[[International Journal of Geometric Methods in Modern Physics]]''. A special issue of the last journal has published a collection of scientific contributions from several Francaviglia's collaborators,<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Journal of Geometric Methods in Modern Physics {{!}} Vol 13, No 08|url=https://www.worldscientific.com/toc/ijgmmp/13/08|access-date=2021-07-17|website=worldscientific.com}}</ref> presented in a workshop in his memory two years after his death.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Workshop: "Variational principles and conservation laws in General Relativity"|url=https://en.unito.it/events/workshop-variational-principles-and-conservation-laws-general-relativity|access-date=2021-07-17|publisher=University of Turin}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Variational principles and conservation laws in General Relativity . SIGRAV|url=http://www.sigrav.org/variational-principles-and-conservation-laws-in-general-relativityvariational-principles-and-conservation-laws-in-general-relativity.html|access-date=2021-07-17|website=SIGRAV}}</ref>

==Monographs==
* ''Elements of Differential and Riemannian Geometry'', Monographs and Textbooks in Physical Sciences, Lecture Notes 4 (Proceedings Summer School on "Geometrical Methods in Theoretical Physics", Ferrara 1987), Bibliopolis, Napoli, (1988), {{ISBN|8870881784}}
* ''Relativistic Theories'' ''(The Variational Formulation)'', XIII Scuola Estiva di Fisica Matematica, Ravello 1988, Quaderni del CNR, Gruppo Nazionale di Fisica Matematica, (1991).
* (with L. Fatibene), ''Natural and Gauge-Natural Formalism for Classical Field Theories: A Geometric Perspective including Spinors and Gauge Theories'', Kluwer Academic Publishers, Dordrecht, The Netherlands, (2003). {{ISBN|978-90-481-6461-5}}, {{doi|10.1007/978-94-017-2384-8}}
